title: CHECK Constraint in SQL
definition: The CHECK constraint is used to enforce rules on column values and prevent invalid data from being inserted into a table.

basic_check_constraint.heading: Basic CHECK Constraint
basic_check_constraint.definition: Ensures that a column satisfies a specific condition.
queries: CREATE TABLE employee (emp_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), salary INT CHECK (salary > 0));

multiple_conditions.heading: CHECK with Multiple Conditions
multiple_conditions.definition: Allows multiple conditions using logical operators.

add_check_using_alter.heading: Add CHECK Constraint Using ALTER
add_check_using_alter.definition: Used to add a CHECK constraint to an existing table.
queries: ALTER TABLE employee ADD CONSTRAINT salary_check CHECK (salary >= 30000);
ALTER TABLE student ADD CONSTRAINT marks_check CHECK (marks >= 0 AND marks <= 100);

when_check_is_applied.heading: When CHECK Constraint is Applied
when_check_is_applied.definition: CHECK constraint is evaluated before data is inserted or updated.
points: Executed during INSERT and UPDATE operations
Helps enforce business rules at database level

interview_summary.heading: Interview Ready Summary
points: It prevents invalid data from entering the table
It can be added during table creation or later using ALTER
CHECK is evaluated before data insertion or update
